anna_dev: FYI Canary showing a noticeable perf regression after today's runtime + Triton/PyTorch bump. latency p95 up ~18% on short-seq workloads, throughput down ~22% on A100 pools.
ci-bot: [perf-check] FAIL — perf change exceeds threshold. gpt2-small seq32 batch8 throughput: -22% (ref: 4120 toks/s -> 3214 toks/s).
raj_infra: ugh. which component bumped? triton? pytorch? driver?
anna_dev: bump set was: Triton 2.8.1 -> 2.9.0, PyTorch 2.2.0 -> 2.2.1, CUDA 12.3.44 driver on canary nodes. runtime merge 7b3c9d7 added kernel-selection heuristics tweak (score normalization).
olivia_ml: quick hypothesis: kernel selector normalization made vectorized matmul score lower for short sequences, so we fall back to generic GEMM. that would explain matmul time up. can you dump triton selection logs?
dan_sre: I reproduced locally on a single A100 with the canary image. pinned sequence=32 batch=8. repro command: \n```\npython perf/bench.py --model gpt2 --seq 32 --batch 8 --rep 50\n```\nprofiled with nsight and see matmul kernel time +34% overall.
raj_infra: paste triton logs from the run (we log kernel id/score).
anna_dev: paste: \n```\n[triton] candidate_kernels: [k0_vec_8x512(score=1.21), k1_fused_512(score=1.19), k2_generic(score=0.95)]
old_score_norm: 1.15
new_score_norm: 0.72
selected_kernel: k2_generic (fallback)\n```
raj_infra: ah there it is. normalization dropped scores by ~40% => selected k2_generic. commit 7b3c9d7 changed normalization to use max-l2 norm across layers. probably unintended for short seqs.
olivia_ml: KV cache behavior check: did we accidentally change cache warmup/skip decisions? falling back to generic could also reduce KV-friendly kernels. check prefix cache hit rates.
dan_sre: prefix hit rates unchanged in canary traces. this is purely compute kernel selection.
raj_infra: bisect plan: revert kernel-selection tweak locally and rerun perf-check. if that fixes, revert in canary. I'll run quick bisect on runtime repo.
ci-bot: Starting perf-bisect job #892 on commit range 7b3c9d7..7b9f2a1
raj_infra: bisect quick result: regression introduced by 7b3c9d7 (kernel selector normalization). confirming: checkout before->throughput 4180 toks/s, after->3208 toks/s.
anna_dev: is there a safe config override we can ship as a hotfix instead of reverting the whole commit? maybe a knob to skip new normalization for short-seq models.
olivia_ml: we can add heuristic: if seq_len <= 64 and batch <= 16, use legacy normalization. tiny patch + config flag `selector.normalization=v1|v2`.
raj_infra: submitted PR to runtime with the flag and defaulted to v1 for short sequences. PR: runtime#4123.
dan_sre: rolling canary update with runtime#4123 now. monitoring A100 canary.
ci-bot: Canary perf-check: PASS on 3/4 nodes, one node flaky but within tolerance. throughput: -2% average, p95 within SLO.
anna_dev: awesome. action items: (1) revert or patch upstream selector? we merged tweak for long-seq fairness; (2) add unit tests for kernel score normalization edgecases; (3) follow-up eval to ensure no regressions on long sequences.
raj_infra: I'll keep runtime#4123 as short-term mitigation. create ticket for a principled selector redesign (link: https://redwood/boards/INF-2321).
olivia_ml: add perf-test for seq 16/32/64, batch 1..16 into CI perf suite so this doesn't slip.
anna_dev: marking rollout blocker cleared for now. thanks all :white_check_mark:
dan_sre: logging note: add an INFO-level line in selector logs when normalization caused fallback so we can alert earlier.
anna_dev: added to PR comments. good catch everyone.
ci-bot: Job summary: bisect -> culprit 7b3c9d7, mitigation PR runtime#4123, canary reverified.
